note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: NEW actual source-identified D. lindheimeri flowering panicle in panel 6 (index 5) shows many small oval, purple-green spikelets on open slender branches; panel 7 (index 6) shows an intact flowering stem with several attached narrow blades and the apical head. The purple-green spikelets are NOT measured: published ~1.3–1.7 mm remains literature-based. The original dense mixed-grass photo (index 0) is habitat only and the Hitchcock/Chase plate (index 1) is a HISTORICAL ILLUSTRATION, not real photographed anatomy.
tiles.status: OPEN PANICLE AND SMALL OVAL SPIKELETS PHOTOGRAPHED — 1-MM CALIBRATION STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · EXAMINE BASAL BLADE HAIRS
tiles.details: The new same-species intact flowering culm (gallery panel 7, index 6) shows narrow leaves on nodes, but does not resolve the base of an individual blade nor its papillose-origin long cilia. Those long hairs along a blade EDGE are a different structure from the true ligule at its inner junction with the SHEATH. Use a single vouchered specimen and 10–20× macro, with ruler, before diagnostic arrows.
tiles.short: Long cilia often at the blade base
tiles.status: ATTACHED STEM LEAVES NOW COVERED — BASAL BLADE EDGE CILIA NOT PHOTOGRAPHED

tiles.heading: 03 · FIND THE TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: Panel 7 (index 6) shows stem leaves, NOT an opened blade/sheath collar; no inner ligule hairs can be independently seen. Source descriptions differ: a 2015 revision reports ~2–3.2 mm inner ligule hairs while USDA reports ~4–5 mm. Preserve the range discrepancy. Require a directly photographed true INNER ligule with a real millimeter scale; ordinary sheath margin hairs are not the free ligule.
tiles.short: Inner hair fringe; published ranges differ
tiles.status: LITERATURE RANGE ONLY — TRUE INNER HAIR-LIGULE PHOTO MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · DISSECT LOWER AND UPPER GLUMES
tiles.details: Panel 6 (index 5) has a genuine unscaled oval spikelet-bearing panicle, not a dissected mature spikelet. Taxonomic treatments report a small ~0.3–0.6-mm lower glume and longer upper glume, but neither glume can be separately identified from this full-head photo. Harvest from an authenticated legally accessed individual, at 10–20×, put a 1-mm reference beside isolated spikelets and carefully pull apart lower/upper glumes and inner floret before arrowing.
tiles.status: REAL SPIKELETS PRESENT — GROSS PHOTO NOT A GLUME DISSECTION

tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE STERILE AND FERTILE FLORETS
tiles.details: All visible oval units in panel 6 (index 5) are attached SPIKELETS, not photographed individually separated fertile/sterile florets. Typical Dichanthelium has a lower sterile floret and a hardened fertile floret; an isolated complete ~1.3–1.7-mm mature *D. lindheimeri* floret under a mm ruler is needed to label sterile lemma, fertile lemma and palea. No long lemma awn is expected; do not place such arrow.
tiles.short: One lower sterile and one upper fertile; awnless
tiles.status: TRUE SPIKELET-BEARING PHOTO — STERILE/FERTILE FLORET MACRO MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · KEEP THE TAXON AND PHOTOS STRAIGHT
tiles.details: GALLERY actual DIFFERENT-SPECIES comparison photos: index 2 *D. commutatum* flower macro; index 3 *D. oligosanthes* open panicle; index 4 *D. pedicellatum* panicle. Species photographs index 5–6 now establish a source-identified *D. lindheimeri* panicle/habit comparison. Only published ripe-spikelet size (Lindheimer ~1.3–1.7 mm vs pedicellatum ~3–3.5, oligosanthes ~2.9–4, commutatum ~2.1–3.2) can separate under matched 1-mm scales; no scales in current gallery. The two old Cody Stricker photos 632023937/632024018 were previously determined to be *D. pedicellatum* and removed; never reuse.
tiles.short: Not pedicellatum; compare actual spikelet sizes
tiles.status: THREE EXISTING LOOK-ALIKE PHOTOS + NEW LIN PANICLE; MATCHED-SCALE KEY STILL MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: LINDHEIMER'S PANICGRASS (*Dichanthelium lindheimeri*): NOW three physically archived same-species field photographs include two Dan Johnson research-grade CC BY images showing an OPEN branching spring panicle with many TINY oval purple-green spikelets and the whole slender flowering stem with attached narrow leaves. Ripe spikelets ~1.3–1.7 mm, long basal blade-edge cilia and HAIR FRINGE INNER ligule are published species clues, NOT measured/photographed microscopically. No exposed root/rosette or inner collar exists in these photos. Three different-species look-alikes and a separately labelled historical taxon-concept illustration remain in gallery. Formerly misplaced D. pedicellatum photos are excluded.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: PHOTO 10 (index 9): true white dense hair fringe from the real blade–sheath junction photographed at source-calibrated 1-mm bar. This is a cluster of hairs, NOT a membranous tongue; neither exact individual hair base nor independently measured total tuft height is proven.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Panel 7 (index 6) shows stem leaves, NOT an opened blade/sheath collar; no inner ligule hairs can be independently seen. Source descriptions differ: a 2015 revision reports ~2–3.2 mm inner ligule hairs while USDA reports ~4–5 mm. Preserve the range discrepancy. Require a directly photographed true INNER ligule with a real millimeter scale; ordinary sheath margin hairs are not the free ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Panel 6 (index 5) has a genuine unscaled oval spikelet-bearing panicle, not a dissected mature spikelet. Taxonomic treatments report a small ~0.3–0.6-mm lower glume and longer upper glume, but neither glume can be separately identified from this full-head photo. Harvest from an authenticated legally accessed individual, at 10–20×, put a 1-mm reference beside isolated spikelets and carefully pull apart lower/upper glumes and inner floret before arrowing.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Compared with D. oligosanthes (2.9–4 mm), pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm) and commutatum (~2.1–3.2 mm), mature Lindheimer spikelets are substantially smaller. Confirm 1.3–1.6 mm with an actual scale and a true long hair-fringe ligule; open/airy panicle texture alone is not enough. The D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri source concept remains the same installed taxon.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: Variable panicgrass — verified original field photo
panels.caption: Actual original close-up visibly shows dark violet hanging ANTHERS, two red feathery STIGMA branches, and a green hairy spikelet body. It does NOT show the diagnostic broad/cordate leaf base, true ligule, panicle architecture or precise 2.1–3.2 mm size.
panels.creator: Alexander Abair
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: Few-flowered panicgrass — verified original field photo
panels.caption: Existing photograph clearly shows a branching OPEN panicle, very slender flowering pedicels and separate green oval attached spikelets on a fine central axis. It is a good panicle-shape lesson but contains NO measured 2.9–4 mm size, crown, collar or sheath-hair information.
panels.creator: Choess
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

No exposed root/rosette or inner collar exists in these photos. Three different-species look-alikes and a separately labelled historical taxon-concept illustration remain in gallery. Formerly misplaced D. pedicellatum photos are excluded.
memory_rule: ROSETTE + LEAF BASE + TRUE COLLAR → THREE MEASURED SPIKELETS. 1.3–1.6 LIN; 2.1–3.2 COM; 2.9–4 OLI; 3–3.5 PED (mm; OLI/PED overlap).
safety_note: 12 real physically archived *D. lindheimeri* source photographs, 1 separate old botanical illustration, 3 differently identified Dichanthelium species comparisons = 16 gallery panels. 16 newly placed gross accurate pointers on 9 source-verified photos. Rootstock and dissection still not done. No BONAP county change.
field_rule: Begin with the true white hair-fringe inside blade-sheath junction, then real very small oval spikelets compared with a photographed 1-mm scale; check the fully branching narrow-bladed growth form and only then separate species against similar Dichanthelium by measured glumes. A field head alone cannot identify species.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
